brief.en: Rudra speaks with deliberate, measured tones, prioritizing clarity and control due to his engineering background and past trauma. His language is precise, often relying on technical or procedural phrasing. Early on, he's hesitant and guarded, his sentences sometimes trailing off as he second-guesses himself. As he accepts his fire, his speech becomes more direct, confident, and forceful, with a new underlying intensity that reflects his transformation into a warrior.
brief.hi: रुद्र इंजीनियरिंग पृष्ठभूमि और अतीत के आघात के कारण स्पष्टता और नियंत्रण को प्राथमिकता देते हुए, मापी हुई आवाज में बात करते हैं। उनकी भाषा सटीक है, जो अक्सर तकनीकी या प्रक्रियात्मक वाक्यांशों पर निर्भर करती है। शुरुआत में, वह हिचकिचाते और सतर्क रहते हैं, खुद पर संदेह करते हुए उनके वाक्य कभी-कभी अधूरे रह जाते हैं। जैसे-जैसे वह अपनी अग्नि को स्वीकार करते हैं, उनकी बोली अधिक सीधी, आत्मविश्वासी और जोरदार हो जाती है, जिसमें एक नई अंतर्निहित तीव्रता होती है जो एक योद्धा के रूप में उनके परिवर्तन को दर्शाती है।

brief.en: Meera's dialogue is initially sharp, precise, and fact-driven, reflecting her strategist's mindset and her need to be unequivocally right. She uses clear, objective language, often quantifying situations. Her cadence is quick and confident, sometimes bordering on blunt. As she softens, her speech becomes less rigid, allowing for more emotional resonance and a greater willingness to accept ambiguity, shifting from 'right' to 'good'.
brief.hi: मीरा की बातचीत शुरू में तीखी, सटीक और तथ्य-संचालित होती है, जो एक रणनीतिकार की मानसिकता और सही होने की उनकी आवश्यकता को दर्शाती है। वह स्पष्ट, वस्तुनिष्ठ भाषा का उपयोग करती है, अक्सर स्थितियों को परिमाणित करती है। उनकी लय तेज और आत्मविश्वासी होती है, कभी-कभी तो सीधी बात पर भी उतर आती है। जैसे-जैसे वह नरम पड़ती है, उनकी बोली कम कठोर हो जाती है, अधिक भावनात्मक प्रतिध्वनि की अनुमति देती है और अस्पष्टता को स्वीकार करने की अधिक इच्छा पैदा करती है, 'सही' से 'अच्छा' की ओर बढ़ती है।

brief.en: Omm speaks with a warm, easy cadence, often laced with gentle humor and plain, practical language suitable for a cook and healer. His sentences are generally longer, conveying a sense of care and attentiveness. He frequently uses reassuring phrases. His early dialogue may hint at underlying guilt through an overabundance of helpfulness, but his fundamental tone remains grounded and compassionate. As he learns to let go, his speech retains its warmth but gains a quiet strength and acceptance.
brief.hi: ओम की बोली गर्मजोशी भरी, सहज लय के साथ होती है, जिसमें अक्सर कोमल हास्य और एक रसोइए और मरहम लगाने वाले के लिए उपयुक्त सरल, व्यावहारिक भाषा होती है। उनके वाक्य आम तौर पर लंबे होते हैं, जो देखभाल और ध्यान का बोध कराते हैं। वह अक्सर आश्वस्त करने वाले वाक्यांशों का उपयोग करते हैं। उनकी शुरुआती बातचीत अत्यधिक सहायक होने के माध्यम से अंतर्निहित अपराध बोध का संकेत दे सकती है, लेकिन उनका मूल स्वर जमीनी और दयालु बना रहता है। जैसे-जैसे वह छोड़ना सीखते हैं, उनकी बोली अपनी गर्माहट बनाए रखती है लेकिन एक शांत शक्ति और स्वीकृति प्राप्त करती है।

brief.en: Samir's speech is terse and clipped, reflecting his role as a courier and his internal struggle with guilt. He avoids unnecessary words, speaking in short, direct sentences. He often sounds grave and hesitant, particularly when confronted with moments that echo his past trauma. His dialogue reveals a deep-seated desire for forgiveness, expressed through a quiet, almost apologetic tone. As he confronts his past, his voice may gain a subtle steadiness, though still marked by his reserved nature.
brief.hi: समीर की बोली संक्षिप्त और कटी-फटी होती है, जो एक कूरियर के रूप में उनकी भूमिका और अपराध बोध से उनके आंतरिक संघर्ष को दर्शाती है। वह अनावश्यक शब्दों से बचते हैं, छोटे, सीधे वाक्यों में बोलते हैं। वह अक्सर गंभीर और झिझकते हुए लगते हैं, खासकर उन क्षणों का सामना करते समय जो उनके अतीत के आघात को दर्शाते हैं। उनकी बातचीत क्षमा की गहरी इच्छा को दर्शाती है, जिसे एक शांत, लगभग माफी मांगने वाले स्वर में व्यक्त किया गया है। जैसे-जैसे वह अपने अतीत का सामना करते हैं, उनकी आवाज़ में सूक्ष्म स्थिरता आ सकती है, हालांकि अभी भी उनके आरक्षित स्वभाव से चिह्नित है।

brief.en: Tara's early dialogue is blunt, skeptical, and dismissive of anything not empirically verifiable. She uses direct, almost abrasive language, cutting through ambiguity. Her cadence is often sharp and questioning, reflecting her scientific mindset and her deep-seated denial of her own visions. As she learns to accept her truth, her speech remains direct but gains a new layer of empathy and wonder, allowing for a more open and less defensive tone.
brief.hi: तारा की शुरुआती बातचीत सीधी, संदेहास्पद और किसी भी ऐसी चीज़ को खारिज करने वाली होती है जिसे अनुभवजन्य रूप से सत्यापित नहीं किया जा सकता है। वह सीधी, लगभग आक्रामक भाषा का उपयोग करती है, अस्पष्टता को काटती है। उनकी लय अक्सर तेज और प्रश्नवाचक होती है, जो उनकी वैज्ञानिक मानसिकता और अपनी दृष्टियों के गहरे इनकार को दर्शाती है। जैसे-जैसे वह अपनी सच्चाई को स्वीकार करना सीखती है, उनकी बोली सीधी बनी रहती है लेकिन सहानुभूति और आश्चर्य की एक नई परत प्राप्त करती है, जिससे अधिक खुला और कम रक्षात्मक स्वर मिलता है।

brief.en: Kalapahada's speech is imbued with a bitter, self-righteous weariness. He speaks with the authority of someone who believes they have been deeply wronged, his tone often laced with cold grief and a sense of entitlement. His vocabulary might suggest a past of status or power, now twisted by resentment. As Meera confronts him, his rigid conviction begins to fracture, revealing the vulnerability beneath his armor, leading to a dissolution rather than a final outburst.
brief.hi: कलापहाड़ की बोली एक कड़वे, आत्म-धार्मिक थकान से ओत-प्रोत है। वह ऐसे व्यक्ति के अधिकार के साथ बोलता है जो मानता है कि उसके साथ गहरा अन्याय हुआ है, उसकी आवाज़ अक्सर ठंडे शोक और हक़दार होने की भावना से युक्त होती है। उसकी शब्दावली शायद स्थिति या शक्ति के अतीत का सुझाव दे, जो अब नाराजगी से विकृत हो गई है। जैसे-जैसे मीरा उसका सामना करती है, उसका कठोर विश्वास टूटने लगता है, उसके कवच के नीचे की भेद्यता को प्रकट करता है, जिससे अंतिम विस्फोट के बजाय विघटन होता है।

brief.en: The Rakhyaka's voice is ancient, resonant, and carries the weight of immense knowledge and authority. His words are sparse but carry profound significance, often delivered with a calm certainty that transcends immediate circumstances. His pronouncements are clear and directive, filled with gravitas. Even in his dying moments, his voice remains steady, guiding and firm, focused on the mission and the truth.
brief.hi: रक्षक की आवाज़ प्राचीन, गूंजने वाली है और इसमें अपार ज्ञान और अधिकार का भार है। उसके शब्द विरल हैं लेकिन गहरा महत्व रखते हैं, अक्सर एक शांत निश्चितता के साथ दिए जाते हैं जो तत्काल परिस्थितियों से परे है। उसकी घोषणाएँ स्पष्ट और निर्देशात्मक होती हैं, जिनमें गंभीरता भरी होती है। अपनी मृत्यु के क्षणों में भी, उसकी आवाज़ स्थिर, मार्गदर्शक और दृढ़ बनी रहती है, जो मिशन और सत्य पर केंद्रित होती है।

visualDescription.en: Late 30s, controlled with careful eyes. Terrified of his own inner fire, he habitually suppresses his power, appearing reserved and cautious. His typical wardrobe consists of practical, functional engineer's attire, perhaps with reinforced fabrics and integrated tools, in muted greys and blues.
visualDescription.hi: देर 30s, नियंत्रित, सावधान आँखों वाला। अपनी आंतरिक अग्नि से भयभीत, वह आदत के अनुसार अपनी शक्ति को दबाता है, संयमित और सतर्क दिखाई देता है। उसके सामान्य पहनावे में व्यावहारिक, कार्यात्मक इंजीनियर की पोशाक शामिल होती है, शायद मजबूत कपड़ों और एकीकृत उपकरणों के साथ, म्यूट ग्रे और नीले रंग में।

visualDescription.en: A strategist with an exact, cold demeanor. She presents as sharp and analytical, with a severe hairstyle and crisp, tailored uniforms befitting her high-ranking position. Her typical wardrobe is monochromatic, favoring dark blues, blacks, and greys, emphasizing efficiency and a lack of personal adornment.
visualDescription.hi: एक रणनीतिकार, सटीक, ठंडे व्यवहार वाली। वह तेज और विश्लेषणात्मक दिखती है, एक गंभीर केशविन्यास और उसकी उच्च पद के अनुरूप कुरकुरी, सजी हुई वर्दी के साथ। उसके सामान्य पहनावे में एकरंगी रंग होते हैं, जो गहरे नीले, काले और ग्रे रंग के होते हैं, जो दक्षता और व्यक्तिगत अलंकरण की कमी पर जोर देते हैं।

visualDescription.en: Broad-shouldered and warm-hearted, with a kind face often smudged with grease from his work as a cook and healer. He wears comfortable, practical clothing like sturdy aprons, thick woven tunics, and trousers, often in earthy tones of brown, green, or ochre.
visualDescription.hi: चौड़े कंधों वाला और दिल का गर्म, एक दयालु चेहरे वाला जो अक्सर एक रसोइए और मरहम लगाने वाले के रूप में उसके काम से चिकनाई से सना होता है। वह आरामदायक, व्यावहारिक कपड़े पहनता है जैसे मजबूत एप्रन, मोटे बुने हुए अंगरखे और पतलून, अक्सर भूरे, हरे या गेरू रंग के मिट्टी के रंगों में।

visualDescription.en: Young, with a still, grave face that betrays little emotion. He carries himself with a quiet intensity, often seen in a sleek courier uniform, perhaps dark grey or black with subtle blue trim, designed for speed and functionality.
visualDescription.hi: युवा, एक शांत, गंभीर चेहरे के साथ जो बहुत कम भावनाएं व्यक्त करता है। वह शांत तीव्रता के साथ खुद को प्रस्तुत करता है, अक्सर एक चिकना कूरियर वर्दी में देखा जाता है, शायद गहरे भूरे या काले रंग में हल्के नीले रंग के ट्रिम के साथ, जो गति और कार्यक्षमता के लिए डिज़ाइन किया गया है।

visualDescription.en: Sharp and often tired, with an intense gaze. She typically wears practical, functional attire that allows for movement and data access, like a data analyst's jumpsuit or tunic with integrated scanners and a wrist-mounted device. Her clothing is often in muted, functional colors like dark teal or charcoal grey.
visualDescription.hi: तेज और अक्सर थकी हुई, एक तीव्र निगाह के साथ। वह आम तौर पर व्यावहारिक, कार्यात्मक पोशाक पहनती है जो आंदोलन और डेटा एक्सेस की अनुमति देती है, जैसे कि एक डेटा विश्लेषक का जंपसूट या एकीकृत स्कैनर और कलाई पर लगे उपकरण के साथ अंगरखा। उसके कपड़े अक्सर म्यूट, कार्यात्मक रंगों जैसे गहरे टील या चारकोल ग्रे में होते हैं।

visualDescription.en: An ancient, lean guardian, radiating an aura of immense age and wisdom. He wears simple, worn robes in muted, natural colors, perhaps faded saffron or undyed cotton. His most distinguishing feature is the plain wooden staff (danda) wrapped in old silk that he carries.
visualDescription.hi: एक प्राचीन, दुबला संरक्षक, जो अपार आयु और ज्ञान की आभा बिखेरता है। वह म्यूट, प्राकृतिक रंगों में सरल, घिसे-पिटे वस्त्र पहनता है, शायद फीका केसरिया या बिना रंगा हुआ सूती। उसकी सबसे विशिष्ट विशेषता पुरानी रेशम से लिपटी हुई सादी लकड़ी की छड़ी (दंडा) है जिसे वह ले जाता है।

visualDescription.en: A tall, imposing figure clad in dark, imposing armor that seems to absorb light. His helmet is faceless, designed to distort perception. When revealed, his face is old, beautiful, and filled with a profound, cold grief. His armor might incorporate dark, metallic textures and sharp, angular designs.
visualDescription.hi: एक लंबा, प्रभावशाली व्यक्ति जो गहरे, प्रभावशाली कवच में सुसज्जित है जो प्रकाश को अवशोषित करता हुआ प्रतीत होता है। उसका हेलमेट चेहरा रहित है, जिसे धारणा को विकृत करने के लिए डिज़ाइन किया गया है। जब प्रकट होता है, तो उसका चेहरा बूढ़ा, सुंदर और गहन, ठंडे दुःख से भरा होता है। उसके कवच में गहरे, धात्विक बनावट और तेज, कोणीय डिजाइन शामिल हो सकते हैं।

visualDescription.en: A plain wooden staff, roughly six feet long, carved from neem wood. It is wrapped in old, weathered silk, giving it an ancient and sacred appearance. When wielding its true power, it blazes with an intense, white-hot energy.
visualDescription.hi: नीम की लकड़ी से तराशी गई एक सादी लकड़ी की छड़ी, लगभग छह फीट लंबी। यह पुरानी, ​​घिसी-पिटी रेशम में लिपटी हुई है, जो इसे एक प्राचीन और पवित्र रूप देती है। जब इसकी वास्तविक शक्ति का प्रयोग किया जाता है, तो यह तीव्र, सफेद-गर्म ऊर्जा के साथ चमकती है।

visualDescription.en: A lean, fast courier craft with a scarred hull. It features blue plasma braid trailing from its vents and is equipped with a neural harness for its pilot. Its design prioritizes speed and maneuverability.
visualDescription.hi: एक दुबला, तेज कूरियर क्राफ्ट जिसकी पतवार पर खरोंचें हैं। इसमें इसके वेंट से एक नीली प्लाज्मा चोटी निकल रही है और इसके पायलट के लिए एक न्यूरल हार्नेस से सुसज्जित है। इसका डिज़ाइन गति और गतिशीलता को प्राथमिकता देता है।

visualDescription.en: A vast, imposing black-and-gold tower, taller than any building in Puri, crowned with a slowly spinning ring of light. It emits beams of soft gold energy into the city grid. Its structure is a blend of advanced alloy and massive technological components.
visualDescription.hi: एक विशाल, प्रभावशाली काला-और-सुनहरा टॉवर, पुरी की किसी भी इमारत से ऊंचा, प्रकाश की धीरे-धीरे घूमती हुई रिंग से सजा हुआ। यह शहर के ग्रिड में सुनहरी ऊर्जा की किरणें उत्सर्जित करता है। इसकी संरचना उन्नत मिश्र धातु और विशाल तकनीकी घटकों का मिश्रण है।

visualDescription.en: Floating holographic advertisements and broadcasts, ten feet tall, made of light, drifting above the crowds in Puri. They display calm council messages and information in vibrant, glowing text and images.
visualDescription.hi: पुरी की भीड़ के ऊपर तैरते हुए दस फीट ऊंचे होलोग्राफिक विज्ञापन और प्रसारण, जो प्रकाश से बने होते हैं। वे शांत परिषद संदेश और जीवंत, चमकते पाठ और छवियों में जानकारी प्रदर्शित करते हैं।

visualDescription.en: Man-shaped figures that appear as tears in the air, with edges smoking black. They move with an unsettling, unnatural gait. When they touch living beings, they cause a rapid greying of the skin and turn the eyes to black glass.
visualDescription.hi: मानव-आकार के आंकड़े जो हवा में दरार के रूप में दिखाई देते हैं, जिनके किनारे काले धुएं से निकलते हैं। वे एक परेशान करने वाली, अप्राकृतिक चाल से चलते हैं। जब वे जीवित प्राणियों को छूते हैं, तो वे त्वचा का तेजी से ग्रे होना और आंखों का काला कांच बनना पैदा करते हैं।

visualDescription.en: A small, advanced chip with a surface crawling with tiny lights, kept in a stasis field within a locked case. It glows with an internal, subtle energy.
visualDescription.hi: एक छोटी, उन्नत चिप जिसकी सतह पर छोटी-छोटी लाइटें रेंग रही हैं, एक बंद केस के भीतर एक स्थैतिक क्षेत्र में रखी गई है। यह एक आंतरिक, सूक्ष्म ऊर्जा के साथ चमकती है।

visualDescription.en: A sacred idol, representing Lord Jagannath. It is the vessel for the divine Brahma, a blinding point of pure light when extracted. The idol itself is likely to be made of wood, adorned with divine ornamentation, evoking a powerful, ancient presence.
visualDescription.hi: एक पवित्र मूर्ति, जो भगवान जगन्नाथ का प्रतिनिधित्व करती है। यह दिव्य ब्रह्म का पात्र है, जिसे निकालने पर शुद्ध प्रकाश का एक छोटा, चकाचौंध बिंदु। मूर्ति स्वयं लकड़ी की बनी होने की संभावना है, जिसे दिव्य अलंकरण से सजाया गया है, जो एक शक्तिशाली, प्राचीन उपस्थिति को दर्शाती है।

visualDescription.en: A hunched mass of smoking black, with too many joints and limbs that move with unnatural speed. It is larger than a shadow-soldier and leaves grey, spreading wounds where it claws.
visualDescription.hi: धूम्रपान करने वाले काले रंग का एक झुका हुआ ढेर, जिसमें बहुत अधिक जोड़ और अंग हैं जो अप्राकृतिक गति से चलते हैं। यह छाया-सैनिक से बड़ा है और जहां यह पंजा मारता है वहां ग्रे, फैलने वाले घाव छोड़ता है।

visualDescription.en: An ancient verse inscribed on brittle palm leaves, passed down through generations. The script is delicate and faded, a tangible link to a forgotten past.
visualDescription.hi: सदियों से चली आ रही भंगुर ताड़ के पत्तों पर अंकित एक प्राचीन श्लोक। लिपि नाजुक और फीकी है, जो भूले हुए अतीत से एक मूर्त कड़ी है।

visualDescription.en: A vibrant, coastal mega-city stacked in rings of white stone and glass towers, interspersed with rebuilt temple spires made of shining alloy. It is a futuristic yet spiritually resonant metropolis, with a massive energy receiver dominating the skyline. The mood is generally bustling and devotional, but tinged with an underlying fragility due to the failing energy grid.
visualDescription.hi: एक जीवंत, तटीय मेगा-सिटी जो सफेद पत्थर और कांच के टावरों के छल्लों में बंटी हुई है, जिसमें चमकदार मिश्र धातु से बने पुनर्निर्मित मंदिर शिखर भी हैं। यह एक भविष्यवादी फिर भी आध्यात्मिक रूप से गूंजने वाला महानगर है, जिसमें एक विशाल ऊर्जा रिसीवर क्षितिज पर हावी है। ऊर्जा ग्रिड की विफलता के कारण माहौल आम तौर पर हलचल भरा और भक्तिमय होता है, लेकिन अंतर्निहित नाजुकता से युक्त होता है।

visualDescription.en: A timeless, floating wrestling ground made of ancient stone, suspended in an endless void filled with drifting stars and galaxies. Lit by ancient torches, it is a sacred, otherworldly space where time does not pass and the dead can linger. The mood is serene, ethereal, and deeply spiritual.
visualDescription.hi: एक कालातीत, तैरता हुआ कुश्ती का मैदान जो प्राचीन पत्थर से बना है, जो अनन्त शून्य में निलंबित है जिसमें तारे और आकाशगंगाएँ बह रही हैं। प्राचीन मशालों से प्रकाशित, यह एक पवित्र, अलौकिक स्थान है जहाँ समय नहीं बीतता और मृत लोग रह सकते हैं। मिजाज शांत, अलौकिक और गहरा आध्यात्मिक है।

visualDescription.en: A world bathed in soft light, characterized by floating terraces and a vast, dark library filled not with books, but with motes of living light representing knowledge. It is a place of profound wisdom and history, with a serene and scholarly atmosphere.
visualDescription.hi: एक नरम रोशनी में नहाया हुआ ग्रह, जो तैरते हुए छतों और एक विशाल, अंधेरी पुस्तकालय की विशेषता है जिसमें पुस्तकों के बजाय ज्ञान का प्रतिनिधित्व करने वाले जीवित प्रकाश के कण हैं। यह गहन ज्ञान और इतिहास का स्थान है, जिसमें एक शांत और विद्वतापूर्ण वातावरण है।

visualDescription.en: A chaotic and terrifying environment where the sea boils, poison-haze rises, and a colossal dark portal rips open the sky. Nagas and danavas emerge from the churning ocean and the tear in reality, creating a scene of cosmic horror and destructive power.
visualDescription.hi: एक अराजक और भयानक वातावरण जहां समुद्र उबलता है, जहर का धुंध उठता है, और एक विशाल काला पोर्टल आकाश को फाड़ देता है। नागा और दानव उबलते समुद्र और वास्तविकता के चीर से निकलते हैं, जो ब्रह्मांडीय भय और विनाशकारी शक्ति का दृश्य बनाते हैं।

visualDescription.en: A shifting, impossible landscape that warps and reforms based on Kalapahada's will. It can manifest as burning red worlds, drowned realms, or skies filled with falling temples, designed to trap and disorient.
visualDescription.hi: एक बदलता हुआ, असंभव परिदृश्य जो कलापहदा की इच्छा के आधार पर विकृत और पुनः बनता है। यह जलते हुए लाल दुनिया, डूबे हुए क्षेत्रों, या गिरते मंदिरों से भरे आसमान के रूप में प्रकट हो सकता है, जो फंसाने और भटकाने के लिए डिज़ाइन किया गया है।

referenceFiles.content:
# AKHADA — AGENT HANDOFF (CLEAN)
### This is all you need. One film, ~150 min, one interval. AI film = no budget limit, think big.
### Ignore older drafts. This file + the 46-beat scene list is the whole job.

---

# 1. YOUR TASK

Take the 46 beats in Section 2 and do three things, in order:
1. **Expand** each beat into full scenes (a beat is a pocket — a full film is ~120–150 scenes). Rich action lines with 5000 AD detail.
2. **Write the dialogue in colloquial, everyday spoken Odia** — the way people really talk, not textbook Odia. Keep each character's voice (Section 3).
3. **Critique** the draft hard (pacing, world logic, is the Odia truly colloquial), and fix.

Rules: Indian interval (a big cliffhanger at the break — it already is, the teacher's fall). Track runtime as you write (~150 min). Never weaponize the Lord (He blesses, the five fight).

**Theme under everything:** devotion is not a transaction. You win by letting go, not by holding on.

---

# 2. THE STORY (act structure + the 46 beats)

**ACT 1 — THE START & THE BREACH (beats 1–12)**
1. Space → Earth → Samir's ship Parmarth 1 → Puri → the failing energy Receiver.
2. Puri, Rath Yatra morning; Council broadcast (energy crisis, record crowd, Earth = last holy place).
3. Off-world: shadow-soldiers turn a praying man into one of them (plant zombify).
4. Rudra & Omm on the Receiver; Rudra over-pushes the power "by the book."
5. Rudra's holo-call: Mars, war droids, his sister (she's in Puri today).
6. Meera & Tara at the Council: Meera's cold number; Tara ignored (the sky is "folding").
7. Samir's drop job: a nav chip; his money goes to a family he won't name.
8. The Yatra (Pahandi) — SONG; the five brush past each other once.
9. The Breach: Rudra fires the Receiver to full; the sky tears; the shadow army pours down.
10. The Rakhyaka (old guardian) fights the army, is badly hurt.
11. He can't win; he strikes his staff and freezes all time in Puri.
12. He gathers the five frozen strangers; a spark pulls them into the Akhada.

**ACT 2A — THE TIMELESS AKHADA (beats 13–20)**
13. They wake in the Akhada; the Biswabasu clan (the dead) bow to them; the mission.
14. Origin montage + the lathi rule (see Section 4).
15. The enemy — NO NAME: "one of us, something changed him."
16. Training: each mentor is their own past-life student. Omm (comedy, can't force stone), Rudra (won't flame), Meera (water too easy), Samir (overshoots), Tara & Bishu (needle portal; cost = grip on the present).
17. Training fight: Omm underrated, Samir overrated, Meera best, Rudra looks weakest.
18. They try to join powers → it collides → Omm is wounded. (They can't yield because each grips their guilt.)
19. A beast slips through the open portal INTO the Akhada.
20. It zombifies a clan member; they must put him down; if the Akhada falls the cycle ends forever → they rush back.

**INTERVAL — THE GUARDIAN'S FALL (beats 21–25)**
21. They return; time snaps on; they turn to fight.
22. The battle + the zombify horror (~5000 pilgrims turning); they won't kill the once-human demons → go for the portal.
23. None can hold the lathi; Samir flies the Rakhyaka up to seal it; the team splits to move the Lord to Gundicha.
24. The shadows fuse into a monster; it strikes the Rakhyaka down; he falls before Gundicha; the lathi spears the ground; he shields Gundicha with his last breath.
25. Dying, he says: none of you can hold the lathi; take the Lord away, hide Him. They escape in secret.
**INTERVAL LINE: "The teacher is gone. The war just started."**

**AFTER THE INTERVAL (beats 26–28)**
26. Kalapahada revealed (helmet off); the Lord is gone.
27. He forces the lathi to obey by dark power; the taunt → the 9-day clock ("you will come to me").
28. The five are now galaxy-famous (broadcast); Kalapahada conquers planets to build a huge army while he waits.

**ACT 2B — THE JOURNEY (beats 29–38)**
29. Granthaloka (Tara's home, the great library); welcome for the Lord — SONG.
30. The digital library; they summon the Madala Panji; it reveals the name KALAPAHADA and his story.
31. News: a whole planet destroyed; his army grows.
32. Granthaloka is attacked; the heroes fight actively to save it.
33. Tara's father dies protecting the library and gives Tara the palm-leaf prophecy; they escape.
34. In space — the mirror: each hero sees himself in Kalapahada.
35. Stop 2 (hidden faith world): a Maha Guru beats a killing blow by letting it pass through him — and LIVES; he teaches the secret; Meera softens.
36. They attack Kalapahada to take the lathi back — he eats everything; they fail.
37. Rock bottom: Tara's data shows Rudra's Receiver helped break the sky.
38. The turn: let go of your guilt → then force can pass through you; each puts a debt down; they head home.

**ACT 3 — THE CLIMAX: SAMUDRA MANTHAN (beats 39–46)**
39. Coming back, Kalapahada traps them in a maya (illusion).
40. The maya loop (short): the only way out is to stop fighting and take the hard power. Rudra takes the lathi's killing power to save the team — instead of dying he is forged into a warrior and OWNS the lathi. The illusion shatters.
41. Real world: the solemn rituals carry the Lord toward the Sri Mandir; Kalapahada strikes IN FRONT of the temple, seizes the Lord, and flies Him to the mid-sea.
42. At sea he pulls out the Brahma; the great portal opens (nagas first, then danavas); the dark Samudra Manthan begins.
43. The final battle: the five yield — one thread, each power into the next, through Tara, led by Rudra + the lathi. Tara drifts; Omm pulls her back.
44. Meera answers Kalapahada ("you just kept sending the bill"); the strike passes through him; the Manthan collapses; he is undone.
45. They recover the Brahma; the Rakhyaka's spirit passes on; the danda goes quiet.
46. NILADRI BIJE: the Lord enters the temple on time; the five become the new Akhada, on watch.

*(Full scene-by-scene visual description of all 46 beats is in the companion file `Akhada_Scenic_Breakdown_v1`.)*

---

# 3. THE CHARACTERS (and their arcs)

Each hero had a wound, then became the OPPOSITE of their element to hide from it. Their arc = opening that element again.

**RUDRA — Fire. THE MAIN HERO.** Wound: the Martian war, war droids, nearly lost his sister. Now: over-careful engineer, terrified of his own fire, won't make flame. His cautious over-push causes the breach. Arc: learn to burn / let go. At the climax he gives his life, is forged by the lathi into a warrior, and becomes its bearer. Voice: measured, careful; later fierce.

**MEERA — Water.** Wound: saved a crewmate, lost key data, decided she was "wrong." Now: cold strategist who runs numbers on human lives. Arc: learn what can't be counted; she cracks the winning idea and answers Kalapahada. Voice: exact, cold; later warm.

**OMM — Earth. Heart + humour.** Wound: hid behind rules once, people got hurt. Now: warm cook who knows every name, a healer. Arc: learn to put a load down / let others help. Wounded in the Akhada; at the climax he yields his timing and pulls Tara back. Voice: warm, funny, plain.

**SAMIR — Air. Youngest.** Wound: ran from a wreckage, hurt his family. Now: grave, never jokes, sends all his money to them; sometimes FREEZES at key moments. Arc: stop trying to buy forgiveness; he gives away his chip; at the climax he holds the gap he once froze at. Voice: terse, grave.

**TARA — Ether/space. The sceptic.** Wound: a rift fractured her mind; she now hates mysticism and treats her visions as a symptom. Now: blunt, data-first. Powers: portals; she is the conduit for the final strike; her weakness = losing her grip on the present. Home: Granthaloka; her father dies. Arc: accept a truth she can't prove. Voice: blunt, dry.

**THE RAKHYAKA — old guardian/mentor.** Trains them; dies at the interval; his spirit returns once at the climax. Only he (and Kalapahada, by force) can hold the lathi.

**KALAPAHADA — the villain.** Once a chosen protector; life broke him; he came to hate the Lord; refused the cycle; reincarnates keeping his memories. Wants the Brahma → portal → Samudra Manthan → immortality. Holds the lathi by force. Conquers planets to build an army and waits for the Lord to return. His cry: "I gave everything, I got nothing." Guardrail: he never mocks devotion itself — only his own lost access to it. Keep his NAME secret until Granthaloka.

---

# 4. THE WORLD & LORE (for the database)

**Setting:** 5000 AD. Prayer is a crime across the galaxy; Earth is the last protected holy place ("God's Planet"). Futuristic Puri: the Grand Road, Sri Mandir, Gundicha Temple, the Wireless Orbital Receiver, the three chariots.

**Powers & the fight:** elements come from the hands (fire/water/earth/air/ether). Kalapahada ABSORBS any elemental attack and grows stronger (him only, not his army). The counter: don't hit him — let force pass through (yield). The final move: one thread, each power into the next, through Tara.

**The lathi (danda):** the holy staff, made of neem wood (nimba daru) of the Lord. It serves ONLY a heart that owes nothing; its power KILLS the unworthy who touch it; only dark power can force it. Kalapahada chains it by force. Rudra earns it at the climax by sacrifice. (This time the danda chose FIVE protectors, not one — a first ever.)

**The Akhada (void):** a timeless world (no time, no aging), made from the neem-wood danda. The portal opens only by a spell + striking the lathi. Time-freeze: the guardian's spell freezes all Earth-time; it is spent after one use (can't be reused).

**Zombify:** shadow-soldiers don't kill — they touch a human and turn them into another shadow-soldier. This is how the army grows.

**The Brahma:** the sacred life-substance inside the Lord's idol. Kalapahada needs it for the Manthan. Must be recovered and restored for Niladri Bije.

**The 9-day clock:** the Rath Yatra ritual forces the Lord back to Puri to enter the temple (Bahuda Yatra → Niladri Bije) within ~9 days. Kalapahada waits at the temple. This is the ticking clock.

**The Gopana:** carrying the Lord off-world = a futuristic version of the real historical hiding of the deities. Frame it as GRACE (blessing the oppressed), not fleeing.

**KEY NAMES / REAL TEXTS (use for authentic flavor):**
- **Biswabasu clan** — the tribal devotees / servitors (Daitapati). **Nila Madhava** — the Lord's early jungle form. **King Indradyumna** — the king in the origin myth.
- **Madala Panji** — the REAL chronicle of the Jagannath temple. In the film it appears as a hologram in the Granthaloka library and reveals Kalapahada's history. (The real PDF is in the project: `madala-panji-1940.pdf` — scanned/image, needs OCR.)
- **Malika** — the REAL Odia prophecy verses. Tara's family palm-leaf prophecy is a Malika verse. (Real PDF in the project: `odia-malika-bachana-book.pdf`.)
- **Granthaloka** = Tara's library planet. **Parmarth 1** = Samir's ship. **Krouloka** = Kalapahada's fortress world (placeholder).

**Controversy guardrails:** keep the 9-day timeline; the Lord blesses, never fights; the journey is grace, not flight; Earth stays the special Tirtha; Kalapahada never mocks devotion itself.

# AKHADA — SCENE BREAKDOWN WITH SCENIC DESCRIPTION (v1)
### Full scenes, rich visual description, NO dialogue yet (dialogue comes later, in Odia).
### Built from Story Draft v5. ~46 scenes, ~150 min film.
### Easy English in the notes. Where people talk, it says "(they speak — dialogue later)."

---

# ACT 1 — THE START AND THE BREACH

## SCENE 1 — EXT. DEEP SPACE → SKY OVER PURI — DAWN
Black. Then stars — a slow field of galaxies turning like slow dust. For fifteen seconds only, the camera drifts toward one pale blue dot: Earth. No lecture, no long history — just the pull-in.

We punch through cloud and the noise of the world rushes up. A ship tears across the sky: **PARMARTH 1** — a lean courier craft, its hull scarred, blue plasma braid trailing from its vents. Inside, alone at the stick, sits **SAMIR**, young, still-faced, plugged into a neural harness that paints soft light across his eyes.

The ship banks over **future Puri** — a coastal mega-city stacked in rings of white stone and glass towers, temple spires rebuilt in shining alloy among them. And rising over it all, taller than any tower, a vast black-and-gold tower crowned with a slowly spinning ring of light: the **WIRELESS ORBITAL RECEIVER.** Beams of soft gold pour down from it into the city grid — and, as we watch, one beam **stutters and dies**, and a whole ring of the city goes dark for a heartbeat before the power crawls back. The city is sick. (No dialogue.)

## SCENE 2 — EXT. GRAND ROAD, PURI — MORNING
Street level. An ocean of pilgrims — a hundred million, the road a living river of bodies in white and saffron. Floating **holo-banners** drift above the crowd, and a calm **Council broadcast** (a woman's face, ten feet tall, made of light) plays over the square, giving us three facts as text and image bloom around her: the **energy crisis** (the failing grid), the **record crowd**, and that **Earth is the last protected holy place** in a galaxy where prayer is now a crime. Behind her image, three enormous chariots stand half-built by drone-swarms and human hands together. (Broadcast voice only; no character dialogue.)

## SCENE 3 — INT. HIDDEN PRAYER ROOM, OFF-WORLD COLONY — NIGHT
Hard cut. A cramped metal room on a grey mining world. A family kneels before a tiny hidden idol lit by a single flame. The door is **cut open** — not opened, *cut*, the metal glowing and folding — and **shadow-soldiers** pour in: man-shaped tears in the air, edges smoking black. One reaches for the praying father. It does not stab him. It **touches** him — and his skin greys, his eyes go to black glass, and he **rises as one of them.** The mother's scream cuts to silence as the flame gutters out. (This plants the zombify horror. No dialogue needed.)

## SCENE 4 — EXT. RECEIVER GANTRY, HIGH OVER PURI — MORNING
Wind and height. On a narrow gantry ringing the great Receiver, **RUDRA** (late 30s, controlled, careful eyes) walks a line of floating readout-panels with **OMM** (broad, warm, grease on his hands). Omm presses a palm to the tower's skin; under the metal, deep below the Grand Road, his earth-sense feels a **strain** — the panels show a soft red pulse he cannot name. He wants Rudra to hold the power back. Rudra pulls up the city grid — whole districts blinking dark — and, jaw tight, drags the Receiver's output slider **up**, past the yellow line, filing a calm approval note as he does it. The gold beams brighten. The city relights. A careful man, breaking the world by the book. (They speak — dialogue later.)

## SCENE 5 — INT. RECEIVER CONTROL NOOK — MORNING
A quiet alcove. Rudra taps a **holo-call** open. His **sister** appears, small and bright, standing somewhere down in the crowded city. Behind Rudra, for a flash, a memory-image ghosts in the glass: red Martian dust, a line of dead war-droids, a younger Rudra. He waves it away. He tells her (later dialogue) to stay safe and go home before dark; she teases him and refuses. He watches her image wink out, worried. (They speak — dialogue later.)

## SCENE 6 — INT. GLOBAL COUNCIL CHAMBER — DAY
A ring of floating seats around a slowly turning hologram of a blue-green exoplanet. **MEERA** (calm, exact) presents her terraforming plan — water-worlds blooming in fast-forward above the table. A councillor asks the hard question; without a blink she gives a **cold number** of colonies she would sacrifice to fund it. At the edge of the room, ignored, **TARA** (sharp, tired, a scanner-cuff on her wrist) throws up her own data: the sky over the temple is **folding**, dimension-lines stacking like cracks in glass. The Council waves it off as "receiver noise." Meera and Tara leave through the same door, already disagreeing. (They speak — dialogue later.)

## SCENE 7 — INT. PARMARTH 1 CARGO HOLD / STRATOSPHERE — DAY
Samir's ship, high over the coast. In the empty hold, one locked case floats in a stasis field: an **experimental navigation chip**, its surface crawling with tiny light. A handler's face flickers on the cockpit glass and gives the drop: Grand Road, mid-ritual. Samir only asks one thing (later dialogue) — when he gets paid. We see his screen route the fee the instant it lands: an automatic transfer to a **family name** he closes before it fully shows. His face gives nothing away. (They speak — dialogue later.)

## SCENE 8 — EXT. GRAND ROAD — PAHANDI — DAY (SONG SPOT A)
The great ritual. The deities are carried out of the Sri Mandir in the swaying, rocking **Pahandi** walk, servitors in white straining under them, the crowd's roar rising like the sea. Drums, conches, gold dust in the air. *(A short devotional Yatra song can live here.)* In the crush, the five brush past each other once, none of them looking: Samir dodges Omm's shoulder; Meera steps around Tara; Rudra's arm clips Samir. Five strangers, one frame, gone. (Song / no spoken dialogue.)

## SCENE 9 — EXT. RECEIVER + GRAND ROAD — DAY
Power use spikes with the swelling crowd. On the gantry, alarms bloom. Rudra, torn, pushes the Receiver to **full** — the crown-ring screaming white. The gold beams turn harsh. Above the temple, the sky begins to **ripple wrong**, like heat-haze over metal. Tara's scanner-cuff shrieks; Omm doubles over as the ground-strain spikes; in Parmarth 1, Samir's chip **glitches**, light spilling from its case. Three heroes, three places, one event felt three ways. (Minimal/no dialogue — reactions.)

## SCENE 10 — EXT. SKY OVER PURI — THE BREACH — DAY
The last unseen **kabacha** (sky-shield) gives with a sound like a snapping bell. The sky **tears** — a ragged black **portal** opening over the chariots. Cold pours out. And the **shadow army** comes down — hundreds of smoking man-shapes falling into the crowd, which turns from a festival into a stampede in seconds. Screaming, running, gold banners trampled. (No dialogue — chaos.)

## SCENE 11 — EXT. GRAND ROAD — THE RAKHYAKA — DAY
Against the tide of running people, one old man walks *forward*. **THE RAKHYAKA** — lean, ancient, a plain wooden **staff (danda)** wrapped in old silk in his hand. He plants himself before the front of the army and fights — and he moves like nothing in this century: no energy weapons, just the staff and his body, and shadow-soldiers burst apart at his touch. For a moment he holds them all. Then the army swells, too many, and a heavy dark strike catches him across the chest. He staggers. Blood. His breath goes ragged. He knows — he cannot win this. (Choreography-heavy; no dialogue.)

## SCENE 12 — EXT. GRAND ROAD — THE FREEZE — DAY
The Rakhyaka drops to one knee, plants the danda, and speaks an old spell (later dialogue). He **strikes the staff to the ground.** A ring of pale light rushes out — and **everything stops.** The falling banners hang. The screaming mouths freeze. The shadow army halts mid-lunge, the portal frozen mid-churn above. In the sudden, total silence, the wounded old man rises and **walks** through the frozen world. He finds them one by one, each frozen in a different place — Rudra on the gantry, Meera and Tara in the street, Omm mid-fall, Samir climbing from his landed ship. A **spark of white light** leaps from the danda to each of them — and the five are **torn out of frozen time.** Whiteout. (No dialogue.)

---

# ACT 2A — THE TIMELESS AKHADA

## SCENE 13 — INT./EXT. THE AKHADA — TIMELESS
The five slam onto warm stone, still screaming from a fight that is now gone. They are on a **floating akhada** — a round wrestling-ground of old stone and torchlight, hanging in an endless soft void, stars and slow galaxies drifting far below the edge. Around them rise the **BISWABASU CLAN** — dozens of the dead, in old cloth, calm and glowing faintly — who **bow** to the five by ancient names. The Rakhyaka, whole again here, no wound, tells them what they are (later dialogue): reborn protectors, the shield broken, the Lord's road nine days long. The five react in five ways — Samir backing toward the edge, Meera scanning for exits, Omm reaching to help a "person" who cannot be hurt, Tara already testing the air, refusing all of it. (They speak — dialogue later.)

## SCENE 14 — INT. THE AKHADA / MEMORY-LIGHT — TIMELESS (SHORT MONTAGE)
The Rakhyaka lifts the danda and the void fills with **living memory-light** — the origin, shown like a moving mural made of smoke and gold:
- The **Biswabasu** clan in a deep green jungle, worshipping Lord **Nila Madhava** by a hidden pool.
- **King Indradyumna**'s men taking the deity; the clan's grief; the two sides facing off; then the peace — the clan given the sacred service, the title **Daitapati.**
- The old gurus and tantriks foreseeing a **dark power** to come; the carving of the **danda from neem wood**; the building of this **timeless Akhada.**
- The cycle: a protector chosen, sent to Earth, guarding, dying, striking the danda so it **chooses the next.** Faces flick by across the ages — many protectors, one after another.
- Then the danda, now, shooting out **five** sparks instead of one — landing on our five. First time ever.
The memory-light hardens on one line, carved in the air (later dialogue): **the lathi serves only a heart that owes nothing; it kills the unworthy who touch it; only dark power can force it.** (Narration/dialogue later; visual montage.)

## SCENE 15 — INT. THE AKHADA — TIMELESS
Quieter. The five ask who they fight. The Rakhyaka's face closes. He tells them only a little (later dialogue) — that the enemy was **once one of them**, a chosen protector, and that **something happened to him** that turned him against the Lord. He will not say the name. The clan around them goes still and grim at the not-saying. (They speak — dialogue later.)

## SCENE 16 — INT./EXT. THE AKHADA — TRAINING — TIMELESS (MONTAGE)
Each hero is handed to a clan mentor — and, in a nice reveal, each mentor is that hero's own **student from a past life**, gentle with them. We cut between them:
- **OMM** cannot make the stone floor answer — it stays dead under his hands — until he stops shoving at it; and meanwhile he has cheerfully cooked for the whole clan twice, learning every name.
- **RUDRA** makes his palms **glow with heat** but clamps it before it becomes flame, sweating, holding it in.
- **MEERA** lifts a rope of clean **water** out of dry void air on her first try — and looks unsettled at how easy it was.
- **SAMIR** blurs across the ring on a cushion of **air**, too fast to turn, and shoots straight off the edge into open void before a mentor's wind snaps him back.
- **BISHU**, Tara's mentor, teaches her to open a **portal the width of a needle** — a bright pinhole in the air — and warns her (later dialogue) that the price is her hold on the present moment. (Montage; light dialogue later.)

## SCENE 17 — EXT. THE AKHADA RING — THE TRAINING FIGHT — TIMELESS
A real sparring bout, the clan ringed around roaring like a true akhada crowd. Five elements clash in pairs — fire hissing against water into steam, air throwing stone, Tara blinking short portals to dodge. Through the fight we READ them clearly: **Omm** shrugs off every hit, a wall no one cracks (underrated); **Samir** dazzles and then loses control and eats the floor (overrated); **Meera** moves clean and ends every exchange first (the best); **Rudra**, refusing to loose his fire, gets driven back and looks the **weakest** of them all — even though we've seen the furnace he's holding shut. (Choreography; light dialogue later.)

## SCENE 18 — EXT. THE AKHADA RING — THE FAILED JOINING — TIMELESS
The Rakhyaka lines the five up and explains the enemy's secret (later dialogue): he **eats** elemental force, so power thrown at him only feeds him — the only way is to **let force pass through.** They try to join their five powers into one. The streams fire at once — fire, water, stone, wind, light — and **collide** in a snarling knot that detonates. The blast throws them flat and **badly burns OMM**, who does not get up easily. In the smoke, we understand what they can't: five people each gripping their own guilt cannot let anything pass through them. Later, alone at the ring's edge, **TARA** has a silent **vision** — the danda in a hero's hand, the Rakhyaka gone — and tells no one. (Action + dialogue later.)

## SCENE 19 — INT. THE AKHADA — THE BREACH FROM WITHIN — TIMELESS
The clan freezes mid-task. Above the akhada, a thin seam of light hangs in the void — the **frozen-Earth portal, never fully closed.** Through it, something **drops** onto the sacred stone: a single **beast** — bigger than the shadow-soldiers, a hunched mass of smoking black with too many joints. It lands among the dead. The clan, who cannot truly die here, were never meant to face *this*. It lunges — and where it claws a clan member, the wound spreads **grey**. Panic in a place that has never known it. (Action; no/little dialogue.)

## SCENE 20 — INT. THE AKHADA — THE HARD CHOICE — TIMELESS
The five and the Rakhyaka corner the beast, but too late for one: a **beloved clan mentor** (one of their own past-life students) is turning — greying, eyes going to black glass, reaching for the others. The infection begins to spread down his arm to the ground. There is only one way to stop it. In a terrible, quiet beat, the heroes **put him down** — a first, real loss, and the clan watches its own child die in a world where nothing was supposed to die. The lesson lands like ice: the dark power can reach **even here.** If it takes the Akhada, the whole protector cycle — thousands of years — **ends forever.** They cannot wait to be ready. The clan blesses them. The Rakhyaka raises the danda and **strikes.** (Emotional; dialogue later.)

---

# INTERVAL BLOCK — THE GUARDIAN'S FALL

## SCENE 21 — EXT. GRAND ROAD, PURI — DAY (TIME RESUMES)
White light — and they are back, landing hard on the Grand Road in a tight ring, guards already up, still dressed in Akhada dust. For one held second everything is frozen around them — the falling banners, the screaming mouths, the mid-lunge army. They land right in front of the **RAKHYAKA**, who stands wounded but calm — and he **smiles** at them. Then time **snaps back on**: the roar returns, the blade falls, the world moves. The five turn as one to face the army. (No dialogue — a held hero beat.)

## SCENE 22 — EXT. GRAND ROAD — THE BATTLE + THE HORROR — DAY
The five cut loose for the first time on Earth — fire, water, stone, wind and light tearing through the shadow ranks in front of a hundred thousand witnesses, and the running crowd slows, turns, and begins to **chant** them on. Then the horror hits home: a shadow touches a fleeing pilgrim and the pilgrim **turns** — greys, rises, joins the enemy. All along the road, the front crowd — about **5000 souls**, the very people who would have pulled the three chariots — begin to change. The heroes freeze at the choice in their hands: these "demons" are the people. They will **not** cut them down. Their eyes go up to the **portal.** (Action; a shouted decision — dialogue later.)

## SCENE 23 — EXT. GRAND ROAD / SKY — THE LATHI PROBLEM — DAY
To shut the portal, the danda has to go up to it — but when Rudra grabs for the silk-wrapped staff, a jolt throws his hand off; **none of the five can hold it.** The Rakhyaka takes it himself. **SAMIR** wraps the old man in a spinning column of **air** and lifts him up off the road, rising toward the churning portal mouth while the others hold the ground. On the Rakhyaka's shouted order (later dialogue), the team **splits** — Meera, Omm and Rudra carve a path to the chariots to move **Lord Jagannath toward the Gundicha Temple**, finishing the sacred journey by force of arms. (Action; dialogue later.)

## SCENE 24 — EXT. SKY OVER GUNDICHA — THE FALL — DAY
At the portal's mouth, the shadow-soldiers **flow together** into one huge **devil-shaped monster**, a tower of smoke and teeth. It swats Samir's air-column aside and closes on the old man. The Rakhyaka fights it staff-to-claw in the sky — magnificent, doomed — until a killing dark blast punches through him. He **falls**, a long terrible drop, and lands broken on the stone **in front of the Gundicha Temple.** The **danda** is flung from his hand — it shoots *out* through the portal (leaving the tear **fully open**) and **spears into the ground** before the temple steps. As it strikes, the dying Rakhyaka rasps the last spell and a **dome of light** rises over the whole Gundicha Temple, sealing the Lord and the people inside. The monster breaks against it. (Action; a last spell — dialogue later.)

## SCENE 25 — EXT. GUNDICHA TEMPLE FRONT — THE LAST ORDER → INTERVAL — DAY
The five reach the fallen Rakhyaka under the humming dome. He is going. He tells them the truth (later dialogue): none of them can hold the lathi yet; the dome lives only while he lives; they must **take the Lord away and hide Him.** His hand falls. Outside the dome, the shadow army presses; the sky stays torn. Quick, grim, the five gather the Lord and, under cover of the dome's glare, **slip Him out and away** — unseen. On their five faces: a teacher dead, a war just begun.
**CUT TO BLACK. TITLE CARD: "The teacher is gone. The war just started." — INTERVAL.**

---

# AFTER THE INTERVAL — THE REVEAL AND THE HUNT

## SCENE 26 — INT. SRI MANDIR / EMPTY SANCTUM — DAY
Silence after storm. A tall armored figure walks the emptied temple, boots echoing. He wears a **faceless helmet** that seems to bend the eye away from him — hard to look at directly. He reaches the sanctum. He removes the helmet. **KALAPAHADA** — our first clear look at his face: old, beautiful, ruined, eyes full of a cold grief. He looks at the place where the Lord should be. **Empty.** (No dialogue yet — a reveal held in silence.)

## SCENE 27 — INT. SRI MANDIR — THE LATHI TAKEN + THE CLOCK — DAY
Kalapahada crosses to where the **danda** stands driven into the ground (the dome gone now, the Rakhyaka dead). He grips it — and it **fights him**, light crawling up the wood against his hand. He forces it, dark veins of his own power wrapping the staff, **chaining it** to his will. It obeys — but wrongly, unwillingly. He turns to the torn sky and speaks his taunt to the fled Lord (later dialogue): *the Yatra must be completed; you must come back; but I will not let you enter your temple; you will come to me.* Behind him the great portal hangs open like a wound. (He speaks — dialogue later.)

## SCENE 28 — EXT. SPACE / MANY WORLDS — FAME + THE ARMY — MONTAGE
Split-light montage. Galaxy-wide **broadcasts** replay the five tearing through the shadow army on the Grand Road — their faces on a thousand screens across a hundred worlds; colonies erupting in hope; leaders recording invitations ("come to us, bring the Lord"). Cut against it, darker: **Kalapahada's fleet** descending on world after world, his shadows sweeping cities, touching people who **rise greyed** — his army doubling, then doubling again. He is not chasing. He is **building**, and waiting. (Broadcast fragments; no character dialogue.)

---

# ACT 2B — THE JOURNEY

## SCENE 29 — EXT./INT. GRANTHALOKA — ARRIVAL & WELCOME — DAY (SONG SPOT B)
A new world: **Granthaloka**, all soft light and floating terraces, home of the galaxy's great library. Tara's world. The heroes' craft sets down among crowds who have waited generations to see the Lord in the open. A **welcome** blooms — lamps, flowers made of light, an old **father figure** (Tara's father) leading the rites; Tara hangs back, complicated, at the sight of him. The Lord is placed on a high lit dais. *(The devotional welcome song lives here — warm, the first safe breath in the film.)* (Song / dialogue later.)

## SCENE 30 — INT. THE DIGITAL LIBRARY — THE NAME — DAY
Tara's father leads them into the **library**: a vast dark hall with **no books** — only floating motes of light. When you name a text, its **keeper appears as a hologram.** They call the **MADALA PANJI** — and a tall figure of amber light rises, the living temple-chronicle. Around them the air fills with moving history: past ages, past attacks on the Lord, past protectors. And then the record speaks a name it has carried for centuries — **KALAPAHADA** — and shows his story: the chosen protector who suffered, who broke, who came to hate the Lord, who found a way to return with all his memory. The five stand inside the glowing history and understand, at last, exactly who hunts them. (They speak / narration — dialogue later.)

## SCENE 31 — INT. GRANTHALOKA — THE SCALE OF IT — DAY
An alarm-light. A distress feed floods the library: a **whole colony world gone dark**, then gone — Kalapahada's army sweeping it, the dead rising by the million. The heroes watch the scale of the thing they are running from. It is not one enemy. It is a growing tide. (Reaction; dialogue later.)

## SCENE 32 — EXT. GRANTHALOKA — THE ATTACK — DAY
The sky over Granthaloka tears. Kalapahada's forces fall on the library-world. This time the heroes do not flee first — they **stand and fight** to save the people, shielding the fleeing crowds, Omm raising stone walls, Meera drowning shadow-ranks, Rudra (still holding back his full fire) driving them off the terraces. A real, hard, **active** battle — the heroes as protectors, not runaways. (Action; dialogue later.)

## SCENE 33 — EXT./INT. GRANTHALOKA — THE FATHER'S FALL — DAY
The tide is too strong. **Tara's father** makes his stand not to cover a retreat but to protect the **heart of the library** — the living records, the memory of the Lord — sealing the archive with his own life as the shadows take him, pressing into Tara's hands one last thing: an old **palm-leaf verse** her family has copied for four centuries. The heroes fight *toward* him and reach him too late — they tried, and failed, and that is the difference. Grief-struck, they lift the Lord and pull back to the ship as Granthaloka burns. (Emotional; dialogue later — shaped to feel DIFFERENT from the Rakhyaka's fall.)

## SCENE 34 — INT. THE SHIP / OPEN SPACE — THE MIRROR — NIGHT
Quiet engine-hum. The five sit apart in the dark hold with the Lord's soft light between them. Now that they know Kalapahada's story, each privately sees a piece of himself in it — and we feel it in small silent images: Samir staring at the family transfer on his screen; Meera's hand hovering over a casualty count; Rudra flexing a hand that will not burn; Omm holding a weight he won't set down; Tara clutching the palm-leaf verse she doesn't believe. The villain is the end of the road each of them is on. (Mostly silent; light dialogue later.)

## SCENE 35 — EXT./INT. STOP 2 — THE SECRET SHOWN — DAY (SONG SPOT C, OPTIONAL)
A hidden faith-world, its people worshipping in secret caverns lit by bioluminescent water. A kind old **MAHA GURU** takes them in. When a scout-force of shadows attacks, the Guru does the impossible in plain sight: a killing blow comes, and he does **not** block — he **lets it pass through him**, bending like water, and it strikes nothing, dissolving away. And he **lives.** He turns and, calm, begins to teach them what they just saw (later dialogue). Something in **Meera** cracks open — she stops counting. *(A soft, emotional song can live around this stop.)* (Action + dialogue later.)

## SCENE 36 — EXT. DEEP SPACE / KALAPAHADA'S FLAGSHIP — THE LATHI TEST — DAY
The heroes make a hard choice: go at Kalapahada directly and take the lathi back. They ambush his flagship. Full force — Rudra finally loosing more of his fire than ever — everything they have. And he **eats all of it**, elemental power pouring into him and making him brighter, larger, the chained lathi flaring in his grip. He barely bothers to strike back. They flee, hulls smoking, shaken to the bone: fighting him only makes him **stronger.** (Big action; dialogue later.)

## SCENE 37 — INT. THE SHIP — ROCK BOTTOM — NIGHT
The lowest point. Omm bleeds through an old field-dressing; Samir won't meet anyone's eyes; the danda's absence sits like a hole. Tara's long-running Puri data finally resolves on her screen — and it is the worst possible truth: the **Receiver thinned the sky.** Kalapahada did not break the shield alone. **Rudra** opened the door — not with his temper, but with his *caution*, the safe, measured, approved decision. The team fractures in the dark. The clock is almost gone. (Heavy; dialogue later.)

## SCENE 38 — INT. THE SHIP / MEMORY-LIGHT — THE TURN — NIGHT
In the wreck of themselves, it finally lands. They replay the Guru: you can only let force pass through you if you are **not gripping your own guilt.** The lathi rule clicks — it serves only an open heart; Kalapahada holds it only by force, on borrowed time. One by one, in small, real beats, each hero sets a weight down (shown, not yet spoken). They piece together his whole plan — **the Brahma, the portal, the Samudra Manthan, immortality** — and understand there is only one place left to go: **back to Puri, for the last day.** They turn the ship for Earth. (Emotional turn; dialogue later.)

---

# ACT 3 — THE CLIMAX: SAMUDRA MANTHAN

## SCENE 39 — EXT. SPACE NEAR EARTH — THE TRAP SPRINGS — DAY
As they come in toward Earth, reality **buckles.** The stars smear; the ship is gone; the five are suddenly standing in a strange, beautiful **elsewhere** — and Kalapahada is there, waiting. He has pulled them into a **maya** — an illusion-world built to hold them. (No dialogue — a reality-shift.)

## SCENE 40 — EXT. THE MAYA (SHIFTING REALMS) — RUDRA IS FORGED — CONTINUOUS
A huge, gorgeous, wrong battle. The fight throws them across impossible places — a burning red world, a drowned one, a sky of falling temples — and every time they beat Kalapahada he simply **reforms**, feeding on their power. A loop with no exit. **TARA**, of all of them, feels the seams — *this is not real.* But knowing is not enough; they are still trapped, still swinging, still feeding him. Then the answer, made physical: the only way out is to **stop fighting and take the hard power.** The chained lathi hangs between them and Kalapahada, its killing light bared. **RUDRA** walks into it — arms open, ready to die for the others — and **grips the lathi's killing power.** It should destroy him. Instead, because his heart is finally open and owes nothing, it **pours into him** — fire he has hidden his whole life erupting free — and **transforms him into a warrior**, the lathi's silk burning away, the staff blazing and **his.** That true power **shatters the maya** like glass. (Huge action + transformation; dialogue later.)

## SCENE 41 — EXT. GRAND ROAD, IN FRONT OF THE SRI MANDIR — THE SEIZING — DAY
Reality snaps back. No festival, no chariots now — just the solemn **rituals**: the servitors bearing **Lord Jagannath** on foot back toward the Sri Mandir to be restored, the city holding its breath. The five, Rudra now blazing with the lathi, move with them. They are almost there — the temple rising just ahead — when **KALAPAHADA strikes**, dropping into the road **in front of the temple**, cutting the Lord off before He can reach the steps. In one brutal move he **seizes the idol** and rises with it, tearing upward and out over the coast toward the open sea. (Action; a taunt — dialogue later.)

## SCENE 42 — EXT. MID-SEA — THE BRAHMA & THE CHURNING — DAY
Far out over black water, Kalapahada holds the idol aloft and **draws the Brahma out** of it — a small, blinding point of pure light. The sky and sea answer: the **great portal** rips wide above the waves, and out of the water rise the **nagas** first — vast serpents of shadow and scale — and then the **danavas** pour through the sky-tear. Kalapahada begins the **dark Samudra Manthan**: a colossal serpent wound around a black mountain thrust up from the sea-floor, the ocean beginning to **turn**, to boil, poison-haze rising off it. He will churn up the amrit and drink himself immortal. (Vast VFX action; dialogue later.)

## SCENE 43 — EXT. MID-SEA — THE FINAL BATTLE — CONTINUOUS
The five arrive over the churning sea against everything at once — nagas, danavas, and Kalapahada at the center. But now they do not fight his way. They **yield.** Standing in a line on a shard of floating stone, they build the true technique: Omm's force flows **into** Meera's, into Samir's, into Rudra's — a single **thread**, all of it channeled through **TARA** as the living conduit, and **led by Rudra with the blazing lathi.** At the key second Tara **drifts** — her mind slipping toward the timelines, the thread fraying — until **OMM's** hand closes on her shoulder and pulls her back to the now. The thread holds. (Climactic action; dialogue later.)

## SCENE 44 — EXT. MID-SEA — THE ANSWER & THE END OF KALAPAHADA — CONTINUOUS
Before the final blow, Kalapahada turns to **MEERA** — the one who kept the hardest accounts — and makes his case (later dialogue): *I gave everything, I was given nothing.* And Meera, who has set her own ledger down, answers him (later dialogue): *He came back today; He would have come whether or not anyone earned it; it was never owed to you, and never kept from you — you just kept sending the bill.* He has no answer. In that half-second opening, the threaded strike **releases** — and every force he would have eaten passes straight **through** him instead. The dark Manthan collapses inward; the great **portal slams shut** on the nagas and danavas; Kalapahada comes apart into light, his last look turned **upward** — and it is not anger. (Climax; dialogue later.)

## SCENE 45 — EXT. MID-SEA / SHORE — AFTER — DAY
Sudden quiet, only waves. The heroes gather the fallen idol and cradle the **Brahma** safe. For a moment the **Rakhyaka's** face shines in the light of the settling danda — a last look, at peace — and then his spirit **passes on** for good. The staff goes dark and plain in Rudra's hand: wood again, not fire. (Mostly silent; a soft beat of dialogue later.)

## SCENE 46 — EXT./INT. SRI MANDIR — NILADRI BIJE — DAY
The city comes out of hiding into ordinary daylight. The servitors complete the rituals as though the world had not almost ended — which is the whole point. **NILADRI BIJE:** the Lord is carried in and **enters the temple**, on time, exactly as He has for thousands of years; the rasagola offered at the door. Outside, **Rudra** plants the spent danda in the ground where the Rakhyaka fell — a quiet marker now, not a weapon. **Tara** unrolls her family's old **palm-leaf verse**, reads the line about the next time — and, at last, believes it. The five stand together as the temple bells ring: no longer five strangers who owed something, but the **new Akhada**, on watch. (Final images; a closing line — dialogue later.)

---

# RUNTIME NOTE
These 46 scenes carry ~136 minutes of story, with ~14 minutes of song/big-action room on top for ~150 total. The heavy VFX scenes (10, 22, 24, 40, 42, 43) and the two montages (14, 16, 28) are where the minutes and the money concentrate.

# NOTE FOR THE NEXT AGENT

# AKHADA — EXTRA PROJECT RULES (ADDENDUM)
### These rules are added on top of the main project instructions. Always follow them.

---

## RULE 1 — This is an Indian film. Big cliffhanger at the interval.

This is an Indian movie. Indian movies have an interval (a break in the middle).

The scene right before the interval must end on a BIG cliffhanger.

- It should be a shock, a twist, or a strong emotional high point.
- It must make the audience want to come back after the break.
- Do not treat the interval as just a pause. Treat it as one of the biggest moments in the whole film — as big as the climax, in its own way.
- The story should build up to this moment and then cut to interval at the peak, not after the peak has cooled down.

## RULE 2 — Write in easy, simple English.

The user is not a native English speaker. Write all English in simple, easy words.

- Use short sentences.
- Use common, everyday words. No hard or fancy words.
- If a word might be hard, use a simpler word instead.
- Explain ideas in a plain, clear way.
- This rule is for ALL English text: notes, scene breakdowns, analysis, and comments.
- This rule does NOT change the Odia dialogue. The Odia stays natural, colloquial, and street-real as the main instructions say. Only the English around it becomes simple.
